title: Estar — place and feeling
practiceFocus: Describe where you are and how you feel

points.title: Who you are, or where and how you are now
points.rule: Ser is still identity and origin: soy ingeniero, soy de Londres. Day 8 used está for where a place is. Today the same verb has five forms for people: estoy, estás, está, estamos, están. Use them for where someone is and how they feel right now. Estoy bien from day 1 is this pattern. Cansado or cansada matches you, the same -o or -a agreement as day 6.

grammar.notYet: The rarer ser and estar contrasts. La sopa está caliente can stay a chunk.

phrases.note: Say cansada if you use feminine agreement.
The day 1 chunk, now part of estar.

phrases.english: He or she is happy today.

phrases.note: The same está as the directions on day 8.

phrases.spanish: Soy ingeniero, pero ahora estoy de vacaciones.
phrases.english: I am an engineer, but now I am on holiday.
The soup is hot right now.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Estoy en casa. Estoy un poco cansado.
lines.english: I am at home. I am a bit tired.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.english: No. And you? How are you?

lines.speaker: Inés
lines.spanish: Estoy bien. Estoy en el parque con mis amigos.
lines.english: I am well. I am in the park with my friends.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Eres muy sociable. Yo estoy tranquilo hoy.
lines.english: You are very sociable. I am calm today.

practice.title: Place and feeling
practice.instruction: Say where you are, how you feel, and contrast one ser fact with one estar moment.
tips: Ser is who you are. Estar is where you are and how you feel.
Cansado or cansada agrees with you.
